subject: Staggered commit + temporary rebate proposal for Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmeanalytics.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exploring a staggered commit + short-term rebate to pilot Redwood

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We walked the architecture and the perf numbers with our engineering and finance leads. We have a potential path forward but need flexibility on pricing to get to a signed SOW quickly. High level:

- We expect to start at ~2B tokens/month and ramp to ~8B over 12 months.
- Procurement prefers a commit schedule with breakpoints rather than a flat annual commit.
- To accelerate our internal approval, they'd like a 3–6 month rebate/credit if usage in early months undershoots the committed cadence.

Can Redwood offer a staggered commit commitment (quarterly breakpoints) with a temporary rebate covering months 1–6 to offset initial integration risk? If so, can you share proposed rate tiers and how credits would be applied on the invoice? We can share a spend plan — attaching a high level sheet.

Jordan
VP, Cloud Products
Acme Analytics

Attachments: Acme_Spend_Plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 13:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring a staggered commit + short-term rebate to pilot Redwood

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the spend plan. I looped in the commercial team to outline options. High level answer: yes, we can structure a staggered commit with a short-term rebate for the ramp window.

I'm attaching our standard hosted ratecard for transparency. I'll propose an initial structure below and then run through internal approvals:

Proposal (draft):
- Year 1 commit: 55B tokens total, broken into quarterly breakpoints (Q1: 6B, Q2: 12B, Q3: 18B, Q4: 19B)
- Per-token list price: see attached ratecard (hosted API)
- Volume tier discounts applied on realized usage per quarter (not on committed amounts)
- Rebate: if realized usage for months 1–6 is below 60% of the committed ramp for that period, Redwood issues a usage credit equal to the difference x (rebate rate).
- Suggested rebate rate: 20% of the price differential (equivalent to a temporary 20% credit on unused committed spend during months 1–6)
- Credits applied on the next invoice as a line item; expire after 12 months if not consumed.

I'll take this to Pricing & Finance for sign-off — cc'ing Ben (commercial lead), Grace (rev ops) and Lauren (sales director). Jordan, can you confirm whether procurement needs credits to be refundable or applied only as invoice credits?

Thanks,
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-ratecard.pdf (PDF)

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Acme — staggered commit + 6mo rebate ask (need pricing committee guidance)

Team —

Acme is asking for a staggered quarterly commit with a temporary rebate for months 1–6. They expect to ramp from ~2B to ~8B tokens/mo. Attached is their spend plan and my draft term above.

Key commercial questions I need from you:
1) Is 20% rebate rate on unused committed spend (applied as invoice credit) reasonable as a standard concession for pilot risk?
2) Do we allow credits to be refundable to a customer (cash) or strictly invoice credit? Procurement asked specifically about refundable credits. Finance historically prefers invoice credit.
3) How do we account for overage billing if they exceed commit in a quarter — do we still honor volume tier pricing on realized usage?

Suggested conservative path (my preference):
- Approve staggered commit but tie rebate to usage thresholds and apply as invoice credit only (not refundable).
- Add a 12-month expiry on credits to limit long-tail exposure.
- Require a monthly usage report and a one-time implementation milestone payment to align incentives.

If you agree, I'll draft the concession letter and route to Pricing & Legal. If you prefer a different rebate rate or structure we can document alternatives to accelerate committee review.

— Sofia

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Acme — staggered commit + 6mo rebate ask (need pricing committee guidance)

+1 to Sofia's conservative path. A few notes:
- 20% feels like a reasonable pilot concession for a strategic logo like Acme.
- Make credits invoice-only — cash refunds open the books to churn risk.
- For overage: yes, honor volume tiers on realized usage; we should ensure ratecard tiers are applied to actual consumption to keep incentives aligned.

One ask from my side: route this to Pricing Committee with an explicit loss-limited 'cap' on cumulative credits (e.g., credits cannot exceed X% of committed value). We should include a clause to revert to standard ratecard if they miss milestones by >2 quarters.

Happy to take ownership of the Pricing Committee briefing.

Ben
VP, Commercial

Sofia — please prep the final concession letter (invoice-credit only, 12-month expiry, milestone payment, revert clause) and attach the SOW-draft-v1.pdf. I'll shepherd legal and finance sign-off post-committee.

Looping in Jordan privately after we have committee language. Let's aim to have a signed SOW by end of November.

Thanks,
Lauren
